Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

lover noun

also lovers, sweetheart, boyfriend, girlfriend, be in love, admirer, lover of (books, the country), be stuck on someone, have a crush on

classical

Ter. And. 3.3.23: amantium īrae amōris integrātiōst (Lewis & Short, s.v. amō)
Verg. A. 4.296: quis fallere possit amantem? (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 282

amāns, amantis m./f.

declension

lover, someone in love

The participle of amāre as a noun: one who is in love, man or woman. Cicero sets it against amātor: aliud est amātōrem esse, aliud amantem (Tusc. 4.27).

Other words

  • amātor, amātōris m. — lover; admirer, devotee (of a thing)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.20: vir bonus amātorque noster (Lewis & Short); Hor. Ep. 1.10.1: urbis amātōrem (Lewis & Short); Traupman 342

    In a good sense a friend, an admirer, a lover of something: rūris, pācis, antīquitātis. Of love between people it is often the gallant or the paramour of comedy; the feminine is amātrīx.

  • amīca, amīcae f.; amīcus, amīcī m. — girlfriend, boyfriend; sweetheart

    declension · also used · classical · Catull. 72.3: dīlēxī tum tē nōn tantum ut vulgus amīcam

    Properly a friend; amīca is also a man’s girl, and in comedy often a mistress or courtesan (Lewis & Short), so it needs a context that makes the sense plain.

  • amīcula, amīculae f. — girlfriend (affectionate diminutive)

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.244: dē amīculā rixātus (Lewis & Short); Plin. Ep. 3.9.13 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 321

Examples

  • amantium īrae amōris integrātiōst

    lovers’ quarrels are love’s renewalTer. And. 3.3.23 (Lewis & Short)

  • dīlēxī tum tē nōn tantum ut vulgus amīcam, sed pater ut gnātōs dīligit et generōs

    I loved you then not just as the common man loves his girl, but as a father loves his sons and sons-in-lawCatull. 72.3–4

  • ego illum audīvī in amōrem haerēre apud nesciō quam fidicinam

    I heard he was stuck on some lyre-girl or otherPlaut. Ep. 2.2.7 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 108

See also love, I love you, romantic, marriage.
